questions.text: राकेश तथा सोमेश एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 2: 3 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे । मोक्ष को फर्म के लाभों में $\frac{3}{5}$ भाग के लिए एक नए साझेदार के रूप में प्रवेश दिया गया। मोक्ष अपने भाग की पूँजी के रूप में ₹3,00,000 तथा ख्याति प्रीमियम के अपने भाग के रूप में ₹6,00,000 लाया। फर्म की ख्याति का मूल्य था :
questions.text_english: Rakesh and Somesh were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 2: 3. Moksh was admitted as a new partner for $\frac{3}{5}$th share in the profits of the firm. Moksh brought ₹3,00,000 as his share of capital and ₹6,00,000 as his share of goodwill premium. The value of the firm's goodwill was:
questions.solution: Moksh's share of goodwill premium is ₹6,00,000 for a $\frac{3}{5}$th share in the firm. To find the total value of the firm's goodwill, we multiply Moksh's premium by the reciprocal of his share: Firm's Goodwill = ₹6,00,000 × $\frac{5}{3}$ = ₹10,00,000. Hence, Option (D) is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: मोक्ष अपने $\frac{3}{5}$ भाग के लिए ₹6,00,000 ख्याति प्रीमियम लाया है। फर्म की कुल ख्याति = मोक्ष का ख्याति भाग × (उसके भाग का व्युत्क्रम) = ₹6,00,000 × $\frac{5}{3}$ = ₹10,00,000. अतः सही विकल्प (D) है।
questions.chapter: Accounting for Partnership Firms - Reconstitution and Dissolution

questions.text: एकलव्य, फतेह तथा गिरीश ने 1 जनवरी, 2024 को ₹30,00,000 प्रत्येक की पूँजी के साथ एक साझेदारी फर्म में प्रवेश किया। साझेदारी संलेख में पूँजी पर 10% वार्षिक दर से ब्याज का प्रावधान था। 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए फर्म ने ₹5,25,000 का शुद्ध लाभ अर्जित किया। एकलव्य के पूँजी खाते में हस्तांतरित की गई लाभ की राशि थी :
questions.text_english: Eklavya, Fateh and Girish entered into a partnership firm on 1st January, 2024 with capitals of ₹30,00,000 each. The partnership deed provided for interest on capital @ 10% per annum. The firm earned a net profit of ₹5,25,000 for the year ended 31st March, 2024. The amount of profit transferred to Eklavya's capital account was:
questions.solution: Interest on Capital is calculated for 3 months (Jan 1 to Mar 31). Interest for each partner = ₹30,00,000 × 10% × $\frac{3}{12}$ = ₹75,000. Total interest for all 3 partners = ₹2,25,000. Divisible profit = Net Profit (₹5,25,000) - Total Interest (₹2,25,000) = ₹3,00,000. Since no profit-sharing ratio is mentioned, it is equal (1:1:1). Eklavya's share of profit = ₹3,00,000 ÷ 3 = ₹1,00,000. Therefore, Option (D) is correct.

questions.text: 'एक साझेदारी फर्म का व्यवसाय सभी साझेदारों द्वारा अथवा सभी साझेदारों की तरफ से किसी एक साझेदार द्वारा किया जा सकता है।' उपर्युक्त कथन निम्नलिखित में से साझेदारी की किस विशेषता पर प्रकाश डालता है ?
questions.text_english: 'The business of a partnership firm may be carried on by all the partners or any of them acting for all.' The above statement highlights which of the following feature of partnership?
questions.solution: The statement "carried on by all or any of them acting for all" represents the concept of Mutual Agency, where each partner is both an agent and a principal for the firm and other partners. Thus, Option (D) is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: यह कथन कि 'व्यवसाय सभी द्वारा या किसी एक द्वारा चलाया जा सकता है', 'पारस्परिक एजेंसी' (Mutual Agency) के सिद्धांत को दर्शाता है। इसमें प्रत्येक साझेदार फर्म का एजेंट तथा स्वामी दोनों होता है।

questions.text: रीमा, मीशा तथा शिखा एक साझेदारी फर्म में साझेदार थीं तथा 8: 7: 5 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करती थीं। 1 अक्टूबर, 2023 को रीमा ने फर्म को ₹5,00,000 का एक ऋण दिया। यहाँ कोई साझेदारी संलेख नहीं है। रीमा के ऋण पर ब्याज लगाने से पूर्व 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए फर्म का लाभ ₹2,15,000 था। शिखा के पूँजी खाते में क्रेडिट की गई लाभ की राशि थी :
questions.text_english: Reema, Meesha and Shikha were partners in a partnership firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 8:7:5. On 1st October, 2023, Reema advanced a loan of ₹5,00,000 to the firm. There is no partnership deed. The firm's profit for the year ended 31st March, 2024 before charging interest on Reema's loan amounted to ₹2,15,000. The amount of profit credited to Shikha's capital account was:
questions.solution: Since there is no partnership deed, interest on a partner's loan is provided @ 6% p.a. Interest on Reema's loan = ₹5,00,000 × 6% × $\frac{6}{12}$ = ₹15,000. Net Divisible Profit = ₹2,15,000 - ₹15,000 = ₹2,00,000. Shikha's share = ₹2,00,000 × $\frac{5}{20}$ = ₹50,000. Option (C) is correct.
questions.topic: Provisions of Partnership Act in absence of deed

questions.text: नीरू तथा पूजा एक साझेदारी फर्म में साझेदार थीं तथा 4:3 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करती थीं। पिछले कुछ वर्षों में फर्म ने ₹5,00,000 का औसत लाभ अर्जित किया । समान व्यवसाय में सामान्य प्रतिफल दर 10% है। फर्म का औसत अधिलाभ ₹4,00,000 था। फर्म द्वारा विनियोजित पूँजी की राशि थी :
questions.text_english: Neeru and Pooja were partners in a partnership firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 4: 3. The firm earned average profits of ₹5,00,000 during the last few years. The normal rate of return in a similar business is 10%. The average super profits of the firm were ₹4,00,000. The amount of capital employed by the firm was:
questions.solution: Super Profit = Average Profit - Normal Profit. Given Super Profit = ₹4,00,000 and Average Profit = ₹5,00,000. So, Normal Profit = ₹5,00,000 - ₹4,00,000 = ₹1,00,000. Capital Employed = (Normal Profit × 100) / Normal Rate of Return = (₹1,00,000 × 100) / 10 = ₹10,00,000. Option (D) is correct.

questions.text: कबीर तथा लारा एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 5: 3 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे । मार्क को फर्म के लाभों में $\frac{2}{5}$ भाग के लिए एक नए साझेदार के रूप में प्रवेश दिया गया। सभी समायोजनों के पश्चात् मार्क को कबीर तथा लारा की संयुक्त पूँजी के $\frac{2}{5}$ भाग के बराबर पूँजी लानी थी। सभी समायोजनों के पश्चात् कबीर तथा लारा की पूँजी क्रमशः ₹8,00,000 तथा ₹7,00,000 थी। मार्क द्वारा लाई गई पूँजी थी :
questions.text_english: Kabir and Lara were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5: 3. Mark was admitted as a new partner for $\frac{2}{5}$th share in the profits of the firm. Mark was to bring $\frac{2}{5}$th of the combined capital of Kabir and Lara after all adjustments are carried out. The capitals of Kabir and Lara after all adjustments were ₹8,00,000 and ₹7,00,000 respectively. The capital brought by Mark was:
questions.solution: Combined adjusted capital of Kabir and Lara = ₹8,00,000 + ₹7,00,000 = ₹15,00,000. Mark's required capital is $\frac{2}{5}$th of this combined capital. Capital brought by Mark = ₹15,00,000 × $\frac{2}{5}$ = ₹6,00,000. Option (C) is correct.
questions.chapter: Accounting for Partnership Firms - Reconstitution and Dissolution

questions.text: प्रखर तथा राजन एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 3: 2 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे, उनकी पूँजी क्रमश: ₹10,00,000 तथा ₹9,00,000 थी। सिद्धार्थ को फर्म के लाभों में $\frac{1}{5}$ भाग के लिए एक नए साझेदार के रूप में प्रवेश दिया गया। प्रखर, राजन तथा सिद्धार्थ के मध्य 12: 8:5 के नए लाभ विभाजन अनुपात की सहमति हुई। प्रखर तथा राजन का त्याग अनुपात होगा :
questions.text_english: Prakhar and Rajan were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:2 with capitals of ₹10,00,000 and ₹9,00,000 respectively. Siddharth was admitted as a new partner for $\frac{1}{5}$th share in the profits of the firm. The new profit sharing ratio between Prakhar, Rajan and Siddharth was agreed at 12:8:5. The sacrificing ratio of Prakhar and Rajan will be :
questions.solution: Sacrifice = Old Share - New Share. Prakhar's sacrifice = $\frac{3}{5} - \frac{12}{25} = \frac{15 - 12}{25} = \frac{3}{25}$. Rajan's sacrifice = $\frac{2}{5} - \frac{8}{25} = \frac{10 - 8}{25} = \frac{2}{25}$. Therefore, the sacrificing ratio is 3:2. Option (A) is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: त्याग अनुपात = पुराना भाग - नया भाग। प्रखर का त्याग = $\frac{3}{5} - \frac{12}{25} = \frac{3}{25}$ | राजन का त्याग = $\frac{2}{5} - \frac{8}{25} = \frac{2}{25}$ | अतः त्याग अनुपात 3:2 है। सही विकल्प (A) है।

questions.text: दीक्षा लिमिटेड ने ₹10 प्रत्येक के 1,00,000 समता अंशों को 10% प्रीमियम पर निर्गमित करने के लिए आवेदन आमंत्रित किए। संपूर्ण राशि का भुगतान आवेदन पर देय था। 3,00,000 समता अंशों के लिए आवेदन प्राप्त हुए। कम्पनी ने सभी आवेदकों को आनुपातिक आधार पर अंशों को आबंटित करने का निर्णय लिया। कंपनी द्वारा वापिस की गई राशि थी :
questions.text_english: Diksha Ltd. invited applications for issuing 1,00,000 equity shares of ₹10 each at a premium of 10%. The whole amount was payable on application. Applications were received for 3,00,000 equity shares. The company decided to allot the shares on pro-rata basis to all the applicants. The amount refunded by the company was:
questions.solution: The issue price is ₹10 + 10% premium = ₹11 per share. The whole amount was payable on application. Total applications received = 3,00,000. Shares to be allotted = 1,00,000. Since no further calls are due (full amount received on application), the excess application money MUST be refunded. Excess shares = 3,00,000 - 1,00,000 = 2,00,000 shares. Amount refunded = 2,00,000 × ₹11 = ₹22,00,000. Option (A) is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: अंश का निर्गमन मूल्य ₹11 है (₹10 + 10% प्रीमियम)। चूँकि सम्पूर्ण राशि आवेदन पर देय थी, आगे कोई माँग शेष नहीं है। अतः आनुपातिक आबंटन के बाद सम्पूर्ण आधिक्य राशि वापस की जाएगी। अतिरिक्त आवेदन = 3,00,000 - 1,00,000 = 2,00,000 अंश। वापसी राशि = 2,00,000 × 11 = ₹22,00,000. सही विकल्प (A) है।

questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.instruction_line_english: Choose the correct option from the following:

sub_questions.text:
'संचित पूँजी' का उपयोग :
(A) कम्पनी के जीवनकाल में कभी भी किया जा सकता है।
(B) केवल कम्पनी के समापन पर किया जा सकता है।
(C) पूर्ण प्रदत्त बोनस अंशों के निर्गमन के लिए किया जा सकता है।
(D) पूर्वाधिकार अंशों के शोधन पर प्रीमियम का प्रावधान करने के लिए किया जा सकता है।
sub_questions.text_english:
'Reserve Capital' can be utilised :
(A) any time during the life of the company.
(B) only at the time of winding up of the company.
(C) to issue fully paid bonus shares.
(D) to provide for premium on the redemption of preference shares.

options.A: कम्पनी के जीवनकाल में कभी भी किया जा सकता है।
options.B: केवल कम्पनी के समापन पर किया जा सकता है।
options.C: पूर्ण प्रदत्त बोनस अंशों के निर्गमन के लिए किया जा सकता है।
options.D: पूर्वाधिकार अंशों के शोधन पर प्रीमियम का प्रावधान करने के लिए किया जा सकता है।

options_english.A: any time during the life of the company.
options_english.B: only at the time of winding up of the company.
options_english.C: to issue fully paid bonus shares.
options_english.D: to provide for premium on the redemption of preference shares.

sub_questions.solution: Reserve Capital is that portion of the uncalled capital which the company resolves to call only in the event of its winding up. It cannot be utilized during the lifetime of the company. Thus, Option (B) is correct.
sub_questions.solution_hindi: संचित पूँजी (Reserve Capital) अयाचित पूँजी का वह भाग है जिसे कम्पनी केवल समापन के समय माँगने का प्रस्ताव पारित करती है। अतः विकल्प (B) सही है।

sub_questions.text:
व्यक्तियों के चयनित समूह को प्रतिभूतियों के प्रस्ताव अथवा प्रतिभूतियों के अभिदान का निमंत्रण कहलाता है :
(A) स्वैट इक्विटी
(B) कर्मचारी पूँजी विकल्प योजना
(C) निजी निर्गमन

sub_questions.text_english:
An offer of securities or invitation to subscribe securities to a select group of persons is called:
(A) Sweat equity
(B) Employee Stock Option Plan
(C) Private placement
(D) Buy-back of shares
sub_questions.solution: Private Placement refers to the offer of securities or an invitation to subscribe to securities issued by a company to a select group of persons, other than by way of a public offer. Hence, Option (C) is correct.
sub_questions.solution_hindi: व्यक्तियों के चयनित समूह को प्रतिभूतियों के प्रस्ताव अथवा अभिदान के निमंत्रण को 'निजी निर्गमन' (Private placement) कहते हैं। विकल्प (C) सही है।

questions.solution: Candidates must attempt either option (a) or (b). See sub-questions for detailed reasoning.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): साझेदारों के वेतन को लाभ-हानि विनियोजन खाते में डेबिट किया जाता है न कि लाभ-हानि खाते में।
कारण (R) : साझेदारों का वेतन लाभ का विनियोग है, यह लाभों के विरुद्ध एक प्रभार नहीं है।
निम्नलिखित में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Partners' salary is debited to Profit and Loss Appropriation Account and not to Profit and Loss Account.
Reason (R): Partners' salary is an appropriation of profit, it is not a charge against profits.
Choose the correct option from the following:

options.A: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परंतु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परंतु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों ग़लत हैं।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is correct, but Reason (R) is incorrect.
options_english.D: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are incorrect.

questions.solution: Partners' salary is an appropriation of profit meaning it is payable only when the firm earns a profit. Items which are appropriations are debited to the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account. Hence, Assertion is true and Reason perfectly explains it.
questions.solution_hindi: साझेदारों का वेतन लाभ का बँटवारा (विनियोग) है जो केवल फर्म में लाभ होने पर ही दिया जाता है, यह प्रभार नहीं है। इसलिए इसे लाभ-हानि विनियोजन खाते में डेबिट किया जाता है। अतः कथन व कारण दोनों सही हैं तथा कारण सही व्याख्या करता है।

questions.text: व्हाइट, शॉन तथा टॉड एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा लाभ-हानि का विभाजन बराबर-बराबर करते थे । शॉन की पत्नी ने फर्म को ₹1,00,000 का ऋण पहले से दिया हुआ था। फर्म का विघटन हो गया । शॉन की पत्नी का ऋण पहले ही वसूली खाते में हस्तांतरित कर दिया गया था। शॉन की पत्नी के ऋण का भुगतान करने पर क्रेडिट किया जाने वाला खाता था :
questions.text_english: White, Shaun and Todd were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses equally. Shaun's wife had advanced a loan of ₹1,00,000 to the firm. The firm was dissolved. Shaun's wife's loan had already been transferred to Realisation account. The account credited to discharge Shaun's wife's loan will be:
questions.solution: Shaun's wife's loan is an external liability. Since it has already been transferred to the Realisation Account, the firm pays it off by debiting the Realisation Account and crediting the Bank (or Cash) Account. Hence, the account credited is the Bank Account.

sub_questions.text: 1 अप्रैल, 2023 को शिवालिक लिमिटेड ने ₹100 प्रत्येक के 7% ऋणपत्रों का निर्गमन 5% के बट्टे पर किया। 31 मार्च, 2024 को ₹1,00,000, ऋणपत्रों के निर्गमन पर बट्टे को लाभ-हानि विवरण से पूर्ण रूप से अपलिखित कर दिया गया। ऋणपत्रों के निर्गमन पर, 'ऋणपत्र खाते' को _______ से क्रेडिट किया गया।
sub_questions.text_english: Shivalik Ltd. issued 7% debentures of ₹100 each at a discount of 5% on 1st April, 2023. Discount on issue of debentures, ₹1,00,000 was completely written off through Statement of Profit and Loss on 31st March, 2024. On issue of debentures, 'Debentures Account' was credited with _______
sub_questions.solution: The total discount is ₹1,00,000 at a 5% discount rate. Thus, 5% of Face Value = ₹1,00,000, which means Face Value = ₹1,00,000 / 0.05 = ₹20,00,000. 'Debentures Account' is always credited with the nominal/face value. Therefore, it was credited with ₹20,00,000.

sub_questions.text: केया लिमिटेड ने 1 अप्रैल, 2023 को ₹100 प्रत्येक के 2,00,000, 8% ऋणपत्रों का निर्गमन 10% के बट्टे पर किया । ब्याज का भुगतान प्रति वर्ष अर्धवार्षिक आधार पर 30 सितम्बर तथा 31 मार्च को देय होता है। 31 मार्च, 2024 को अपलिखित ब्याज था :

sub_questions.solution: Nominal value of debentures = 2,00,000 × ₹100 = ₹2,00,00,000. Total annual interest @ 8% = ₹2,00,00,000 × 8% = ₹16,00,000. The full year's debenture interest is written off to the Statement of Profit and Loss at the end of the year (31st March 2024), which amounts to ₹16,00,000.

sub_questions.text: तविश, उमेश तथा वरुन एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 4:3 : 2 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे । तविश सेवानिवृत्त हो गया। उमेश तथा वरुन ने भविष्य में लाभ-हानि 5 : 3 के अनुपात में विभाजित करने का निर्णय लिया। उमेश का अभिलाभ भाग होगा :
sub_questions.text_english: Tavish, Umesh and Varun were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 4 : 3 : 2. Tavish retired. Umesh and Varun decided to share profits and losses in future in the ratio of 5 : 3. The gaining share of Umesh will be :
sub_questions.solution: Gaining Share = New Share - Old Share. Umesh's old share = $\frac{3}{9}$ = $\frac{24}{72}$. Umesh's new share = $\frac{5}{8}$ = $\frac{45}{72}$. Gain = $\frac{45}{72} - \frac{24}{72}$ = $\frac{21}{72}$. Option (A) is correct.
sub_questions.solution_hindi: अभिलाभ (Gain) = नया भाग - पुराना भाग। उमेश का पुराना भाग = $\frac{3}{9} = \frac{24}{72}$. नया भाग = $\frac{5}{8} = \frac{45}{72}$. अभिलाभ = $\frac{45}{72} - \frac{24}{72} = \frac{21}{72}$. अतः विकल्प (A) सही है।

sub_questions.text: असित, सोनू तथा हिना एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 3:2:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे । असित सेवानिवृत्त हो गया तथा संचयों व परिसंपत्तियों एवं देयताओं के पुनर्मूल्यांकन के लिए आवश्यक समायोजनों के पश्चात् उसके पूँजी खाते में ₹ 40,00,000 का शेष था । सोनू तथा हिना उसके दावे के पूर्ण निपटान के लिए ₹ 45,00,000 का भुगतान करने के लिए सहमत हो गए। फर्म की ख्याति का मूल्य था :
sub_questions.text_english: Asit, Sonu and Hina were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3 : 2 : 1. Asit retired and the balance in his capital account after making necessary adjustments on account of reserves and revaluation of assets and liabilities was ₹ 40,00,000. Sonu and Hina agreed to pay him ₹ 45,00,000 in full settlement of his claim. The value of goodwill of the firm was :
sub_questions.solution: The excess amount paid over the adjusted capital balance is the retiring partner's share of goodwill (Hidden Goodwill). Asit's share of goodwill = ₹45,00,000 - ₹40,00,000 = ₹5,00,000. Asit's profit share was $\frac{3}{6}$ (or $\frac{1}{2}$). Total firm's goodwill = ₹5,00,000 × 2 = ₹10,00,000. Option (D) is correct.

sub_questions.text: अजित, बिस्वास तथा चित्रा एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 5 : 3 : 2 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे। 30 सितंबर, 2024 को बिस्वास की मृत्यु हो गई। फर्म अपनी पुस्तकें प्रति वर्ष 31 मार्च को बंद करती है। पिछले स्थिति विवरण की तिथि से उसकी मृत्यु की तिथि तक लाभ में बिस्वास के भाग की गणना विक्रय के आधार पर की जाएगी। 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए विक्रय की राशि ₹24,00,000 थी तथा 1 अप्रैल, 2024 से 30 सितंबर, 2024 तक यह राशि ₹15,00,000 थी। 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए लाभ ₹2,40,000 था। मृत्यु की तिथि तक लाभों में बिस्वास का भाग था :
sub_questions.text_english: Ajit, Biswas and Chitra were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5 : 3 : 2. Biswas died on 30th September, 2024. The firm closes its books on 31st March every year. Biswas's share of profits till the date of death from the last Balance Sheet date, was to be calculated on the basis of sales. Sales for the year ended 31st March, 2024 amounted to ₹24,00,000 and that from 1st April, 2024 to 30th September, 2024 amounted to ₹15,00,000. The profits for the year ended 31st March, 2024 were ₹2,40,000. Biswas's share of profit till the date of his death was :
sub_questions.solution: Profit percentage on sales based on previous year = (₹2,40,000 / ₹24,00,000) × 100 = 10%. Estimated profit till the date of death based on sales = 10% of ₹15,00,000 = ₹1,50,000. Biswas's share of profit = ₹1,50,000 × $\frac{3}{10}$ = ₹45,000. Option (C) is correct.

sub_questions.text: ईशा, जूली तथा कविता एक फर्म में साझेदार थीं तथा 3:2:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करती थीं। फर्म अपनी पुस्तकें प्रति वर्ष 31 मार्च को बंद करती है। 12 जून, 2024 को कविता की मृत्यु हो गई। पिछले स्थिति विवरण की तिथि से उसकी मृत्यु की तिथि तक फर्म के लाभों में उसके भाग की गणना पिछले वर्ष के लाभ के आधार पर की जाएगी। पिछले वर्ष का लाभ ₹6,00,000 था। मृत्यु की तिथि तक लाभ में कविता का भाग था :
sub_questions.text_english: Isha, Julie and Kavita were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3 : 2 : 1. The firm closes its books on 31st March every year. On 12th June, 2024, Kavita died. Her share in the profits of the firm from the last Balance Sheet till the date of her death was to be calculated on the basis of previous year's profit. The previous year's profit was ₹6,00,000. Kavita's share of profit till the date of her death was :
sub_questions.solution: Number of days from 1st April to 12th June = April(30) + May(31) + June(12) = 73 days. Estimated profit for 73 days = ₹6,00,000 × $\frac{73}{365}$ = ₹1,20,000. Kavita's share = ₹1,20,000 × $\frac{1}{6}$ = ₹20,000. Option (A) is correct.

Total loss on issue = 20,000 debentures × ₹10 = ₹2,00,000. The premium on issue is a capital profit (Securities Premium) and not part of the loss. Option (A) is correct.

questions.text:
अमन, सुमन तथा तन्वी एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 9:8: 7 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे। उन्होंने 1 अप्रैल, 2024 से भविष्य में लाभ-हानि 7 : 9 : 8 के अनुपात में विभाजित करने का निर्णय लिया। 31 मार्च, 2024 को उनका स्थिति विवरण दर्शा रहा था :
(i) ₹24,00,000 का आकस्मिक संचय ।
(ii) लाभ-हानि खाते में ₹12,00,000 का क्रेडिट शेष।
फर्म की ख्याति का मूल्यांकन ₹42,00,000 किया गया तथा परिसंपत्तियों और देयताओं के पुनर्मूल्यांकन से ₹6,00,000 की हानि हुई। साझेदार आकस्मिक संचय तथा लाभ-हानि खाते के शेष को वितरित नहीं करना चाहते थे। उन्होंने यह भी निर्णय लिया कि परिसंपत्तियों तथा देयताओं के पुनर्मूल्यांकित मूल्यों को पुस्तकों में नहीं दर्शाया जाएगा।
उपर्युक्त के प्रभाव को दर्शाने के लिए एक एकल समायोजन प्रविष्टि दीजिए। अपनी कार्य-विधि स्पष्ट रूप से दर्शाइए।
questions.text_english:
Aman, Suman and Tanvi were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 9 : 8 : 7. They decided to share future profits and losses in the ratio of 7 : 9 : 8 with effect from 1st April, 2024. Their Balance Sheet as at 31st March, 2024 showed :
(i) Contingency Reserve of ₹24,00,000.
(ii) Credit Balance of ₹12,00,000 in Profit and Loss Account.
Goodwill of the firm was valued at ₹42,00,000 and Revaluation of assets and liabilities resulted in a loss of ₹6,00,000. The partners did not want to distribute the Contingency Reserve and the Balance of the Profit and Loss Account. They also decided that revalued values of assets and liabilities were not to be recorded in the books.
Pass a single adjustment entry to give effect to the above. Show your workings clearly.

key_points: Calculate net amount to be adjusted: Contingency Reserve + P&L + Goodwill - Revaluation Loss
Calculate Sacrifice/Gain of each partner based on Old Ratio and New Ratio
Debit the gaining partners and credit the sacrificing partner with their respective share of the net adjusted amount

questions.solution:
Working Notes:
1. Calculation of Net Amount for Adjustment:
Contingency Reserve: ₹24,00,000
Profit & Loss A/c (Cr.): ₹12,00,000
Goodwill: ₹42,00,000
Less: Revaluation Loss: (₹6,00,000)
Net Amount to be adjusted = ₹72,00,000

2. Calculation of Sacrifice/Gain:
Old Ratio = 9 : 8 : 7 (Total 24)
New Ratio = 7 : 9 : 8 (Total 24)
Sacrifice = Old Share - New Share
Aman = 9/24 - 7/24 = 2/24 (Sacrifice)
Suman = 8/24 - 9/24 = -1/24 (Gain)
Tanvi = 7/24 - 8/24 = -1/24 (Gain)

3. Single Adjustment Journal Entry:
Suman's Capital A/c ... Dr. (₹72,00,000 × 1/24)  ₹3,00,000
Tanvi's Capital A/c ... Dr. (₹72,00,000 × 1/24)  ₹3,00,000
    To Aman's Capital A/c  (₹72,00,000 × 2/24)  ₹6,00,000
(Being adjustment entry passed for goodwill, reserves, accumulated profits and revaluation loss due to change in profit sharing ratio without altering the book values)

(i) निवेश का बाज़ार मूल्य ₹44,00,000 था।
(ii) कर्मचारी क्षतिपूर्ति के दावे का अनुमान ₹25,00,000 लगाया गया था।

questions.text_english:
Vishal and Pulkit were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 7 : 3. The following is the extract of their Balance Sheet as at 31st March, 2024.
On 1st April, 2024, Tarun was admitted as a new partner for $\frac{1}{5}$th share in the profits of the firm on the following terms :
(i) Market value of investments was ₹44,00,000.
(ii) Claim on account of Workmen Compensation was estimated at ₹25,00,000.
Pass necessary journal entries for treatment of Investment Fluctuation Fund and Workmen Compensation Fund on Tarun's admission.

Distribute the revaluation loss among old partners in their old profit sharing ratio.
Transfer Workmen Compensation Fund to Provision for Workmen Compensation Claim as the claim is equal to the fund amount.

questions.solution:
Journal Entries in the books of the Firm:

1. Investment Fluctuation Fund A/c ... Dr. ₹5,00,000

     To Investments A/c ₹6,00,000

2. Vishal's Capital A/c ... Dr. ₹70,000

     To Revaluation A/c ₹1,00,000
(Being the loss on revaluation transferred to old partners in their old ratio 7:3)

3. Workmen Compensation Fund A/c ... Dr. ₹25,00,000
     To Provision for Workmen Compensation Claim A/c ₹25,00,000

मल्लार्क लिमिटेड ने नरोहा लिमिटेड से ₹40,00,000 पुस्तक मूल्य की परिसंपत्तियाँ क्रय कीं तथा ₹5,00,000 की देयताएँ लीं। यह सहमति हुई कि ₹36,00,000 के क्रय प्रतिफल का भुगतान ₹100 प्रत्येक के 7% ऋणपत्रों को 20% प्रीमियम पर निर्गमित करके किया जाएगा।
उपर्युक्त लेन-देनों के लिए मल्लार्क लिमिटेड की पुस्तकों में रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ अभिलेखित कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english:
Mallark Ltd. purchased assets of book value ₹40,00,000 and took over liabilities of ₹5,00,000 from Naroha Ltd. It was agreed that the purchase consideration, ₹36,00,000 be paid by issuing 7% debentures of ₹100 each at a premium of 20%.
Record the journal entries in the books of Mallark Ltd. for the above transactions.

key_points: Record asset purchase and liabilities takeover, calculating Goodwill (Balancing figure: Net Assets = 35L, PC = 36L -> Goodwill = 1L)
Calculate number of debentures issued: PC / Issue Price = 36,00,000 / 120 = 30,000 debentures
Pass entry for issuing debentures at premium to Vendor

sub_questions.solution:
Journal Entries in the books of Mallark Ltd.:

1. Sundry Assets A/c ... Dr. ₹40,00,000
   Goodwill A/c (Balancing Figure) ... Dr. ₹1,00,000
     To Sundry Liabilities A/c ₹5,00,000
     To Naroha Ltd. ₹36,00,000
(Being assets and liabilities taken over and purchase consideration fixed, excess of PC over Net Assets debited to Goodwill)

(Working: Net Assets = 40,00,000 - 5,00,000 = 35,00,000. PC = 36,00,000. Goodwill = 36,00,000 - 35,00,000 = 1,00,000)

2. Naroha Ltd. ... Dr. ₹36,00,000
     To 7% Debentures A/c (30,000 × ₹100) ₹30,00,000
     To Securities Premium A/c (30,000 × ₹20) ₹6,00,000
(Being 30,000 7% debentures of ₹100 each issued at a premium of 20% in discharge of purchase consideration)

(Working: Number of Debentures = ₹36,00,000 / ₹120 = 30,000)

सनलॉक लिमिटेड की पुस्तकों में रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ अभिलेखित कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english:
Sunlock Ltd. purchased assets of book value ₹50,00,000 and took over liabilities of ₹6,00,000 from Moondock Ltd. It paid the purchase consideration by issue of 46,000, 8% debentures of ₹100 each at a discount of 10%.
Record the journal entries in the books of Sunlock Ltd.

key_points: Calculate PC: 46,000 debentures * 90 = 41,40,000
Record asset purchase and liabilities takeover, calculating Capital Reserve (Balancing figure: Net Assets = 44L, PC = 41.4L -> CR = 2,60,000)
Pass entry for issuing debentures at discount to Vendor

sub_questions.solution:
Journal Entries in the books of Sunlock Ltd.:

1. Sundry Assets A/c ... Dr. ₹50,00,000
     To Sundry Liabilities A/c ₹6,00,000
     To Moondock Ltd. ₹41,40,000
     To Capital Reserve A/c (Balancing Figure) ₹2,60,000
(Being assets and liabilities taken over, PC fixed at ₹41,40,000 and the surplus transferred to Capital Reserve)

(Working: PC = 46,000 debentures × (₹100 - ₹10) = ₹41,40,000. Net Assets = 50,00,000 - 6,00,000 = 44,00,000. Capital Reserve = 44,00,000 - 41,40,000 = 2,60,000)

2. Moondock Ltd. ... Dr. ₹41,40,000
   Discount on Issue of Debentures A/c ... Dr. ₹4,60,000
     To 8% Debentures A/c ₹46,00,000
(Being 46,000 8% Debentures of ₹100 each issued at a discount of 10% to Moondock Ltd.)

questions.instruction_line_english: Attempt any ONE of the following:

sub_questions.text:
अभय तथा सुजोय ने 1 अप्रैल, 2024 को क्रमशः ₹80,00,000 तथा ₹60,00,000 की पूँजी के साथ साझेदारी में प्रवेश किया। साझेदारों ने लाभों को अपने पूँजी अंशदान के अनुपात में विभाजित करने का निर्णय लिया। उन्होंने वर्ष के दौरान क्रमशः ₹6,00,000 तथा ₹4,00,000 का आहरण किया। साझेदारों के आहरण पर 10% वार्षिक दर से ब्याज लगाया गया। सुजोय को प्रति वर्ष न्यूनतम ₹3,50,000 के लाभ के भाग की गारंटी दी गई थी।
31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए फर्म का लाभ ₹6,50,000 था।
31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए फर्म का लाभ-हानि विनियोजन खाता तैयार कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english:
Abhay and Sujoy entered into partnership on 1st April, 2024 with capitals of ₹80,00,000 and ₹60,00,000 respectively. The partners decided to share profits in the ratio of their capital contribution. They withdrew ₹6,00,000 and ₹4,00,000 respectively during the year. The partners were charged interest on drawings @ 10% per annum. A share of profit was guaranteed by Sujoy at a minimum of ₹3,50,000 per annum. The profit of the firm for the year ended 31st March, 2024 amounted to ₹6,50,000.
Prepare Profit and Loss Appropriation Account of the firm for the year ended 31st March, 2024.

key_points: Calculate Interest on Drawings assuming average 6 months period.
Calculate divisible profit and allocate it in the capital ratio (4:3).

Adjust the guaranteed amount. Sujoy is guaranteed ₹3,50,000. Wait, the question states 'A share of profit was guaranteed TO Sujoy' (Hindi says सुजोय को... गारंटी दी गई थी). Thus, any deficiency falls on Abhay.

sub_questions.solution:
Working Notes:
1. Ratio of capital contribution = 80,00,000 : 60,00,000 = 4 : 3.
2. Interest on Drawings (Calculated for average period of 6 months as date of withdrawal is not given):
   Abhay = ₹6,00,000 × 10% × 6/12 = ₹30,000
   Sujoy = ₹4,00,000 × 10% × 6/12 = ₹20,000
   Total Interest on Drawings = ₹50,000
3. Divisible Profit = Net Profit (₹6,50,000) + Interest on Drawings (₹50,000) = ₹7,00,000
4. Distribution of Profit (4:3):
   Abhay's share = ₹7,00,000 × 4/7 = ₹4,00,000
   Sujoy's share = ₹7,00,000 × 3/7 = ₹3,00,000
5. Guarantee Adjustment:
   Sujoy is guaranteed a minimum profit of ₹3,50,000. His calculated share is ₹3,00,000.
   Deficiency = ₹3,50,000 - ₹3,00,000 = ₹50,000.
   This deficiency will be borne by Abhay.
   Final Share of Abhay = ₹4,00,000 - ₹50,000 = ₹3,50,000
   Final Share of Sujoy = ₹3,00,000 + ₹50,000 = ₹3,50,000

Profit and Loss Appropriation Account for the year ended 31st March, 2024:
Dr. (₹)                           | Cr. (₹)
To Profit transferred to Cap A/cs:| By Net Profit as per P&L A/c 6,50,000
  Abhay: 4,00,000                 | By Interest on Drawings:
  Less: Deficiency (50,000) 3,50,000|   Abhay 30,000
  Sujoy: 3,00,000                 |   Sujoy 20,000 50,000
  Add: Recovery 50,000 3,50,000   |
Total: 7,00,000                   | Total: 7,00,000

sub_questions.text:
सोनिया तथा श्रुति एक फर्म में साझेदार थीं तथा 5 : 3 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करती थीं। 1 अप्रैल, 2023 को उनके स्थिर पूँजी खातों में क्रमशः ₹25,00,000 तथा ₹15,00,000 का शेष था। 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए फर्म का लाभ ₹24,00,000 था।
लाभों में उनके भाग की गणना कीजिए, यदि :
(i) पूँजी पर ब्याज के भुगतान के विषय में साझेदारी संलेख मौन है।
(ii) साझेदारी संलेख में पूँजी पर 10% वार्षिक दर से ब्याज का प्रावधान है।
sub_questions.text_english:
Sonia and Shruti were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5 : 3. On 1st April, 2023 the balance in their fixed capital accounts were ₹25,00,000 and ₹15,00,000 respectively. The profit of the firm for the year ended 31st March, 2024 was ₹24,00,000.
Calculate their share of profit if :
(i) the partnership deed is silent as to the payment of interest on capital.
(ii) the partnership deed provides for interest on capital @ 10% per annum.

key_points: Case (i): When deed is silent, no Interest on Capital is allowed. Distribute entire profit ₹24,00,000 in 5:3 ratio.
Case (ii): Provide Interest on Capital at 10%. Subtract it from Net Profit. Distribute remaining profit in 5:3 ratio.

sub_questions.solution:
Case (i): If the partnership deed is silent, no interest on capital is allowed.
Divisible Profit = ₹24,00,000.
Sonia's share of profit = ₹24,00,000 × (5/8) = ₹15,00,000.
Shruti's share of profit = ₹24,00,000 × (3/8) = ₹9,00,000.

Case (ii): If the partnership deed provides for interest on capital @ 10% p.a.
Interest on Sonia's Capital = 10% of ₹25,00,000 = ₹2,50,000.
Interest on Shruti's Capital = 10% of ₹15,00,000 = ₹1,50,000.
Total Interest on Capital = ₹2,50,000 + ₹1,50,000 = ₹4,00,000.
Divisible Profit = Net Profit - Total Interest on Capital = ₹24,00,000 - ₹4,00,000 = ₹20,00,000.
Sonia's share of profit = ₹20,00,000 × (5/8) = ₹12,50,000.
Shruti's share of profit = ₹20,00,000 × (3/8) = ₹7,50,000.

questions.solution: Candidates must attempt either option (a) or (b). See sub-questions for detailed reasoning.

सीडी लिमिटेड ने ₹100 प्रत्येक के 2,000, 12% ऋणपत्रों को ₹10 प्रति ऋणपत्र के प्रीमियम पर निर्गमित करने के लिए आवेदन आमंत्रित किए। राशि निम्न प्रकार से देय थी :

सीडी लिमिटेड की पुस्तकों में उपर्युक्त लेन-देनों के लिए आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ दीजिए।
questions.text_english:
CD Ltd. invited applications for issuing 2,000, 12% debentures of ₹100 each at a premium of ₹10 per debenture. The amount was payable as follows :
On Application - ₹50 per debenture
On Allotment - ₹60 per debenture (including premium)
The debentures were fully subscribed, and all money was duly received.
Pass necessary journal entries for the above transactions in the books of CD Ltd.

key_points: Record receipt of application money: Bank to Debenture Application (2,000 * 50).
Transfer application money to Debentures A/c.
Make allotment money due along with Securities Premium: Debenture Allotment to Debentures A/c & Securities Premium A/c.
Record receipt of allotment money: Bank to Debenture Allotment (2,000 * 60).

questions.solution:
Journal Entries in the books of CD Ltd.:

     To Debenture Application A/c ₹1,00,000
(Being application money received on 2,000 debentures @ ₹50 per debenture)

2. Debenture Application A/c ... Dr. ₹1,00,000
     To 12% Debentures A/c ₹1,00,000
(Being application money transferred to 12% Debentures Account)

3. Debenture Allotment A/c ... Dr. ₹1,20,000
     To 12% Debentures A/c ₹1,00,000

4. Bank A/c ... Dr. ₹1,20,000

(Being allotment money duly received)

गोपाल, हीरा तथा इकबाल एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा लाभ-हानि बराबर-बराबर बाँटते थे । 1 अप्रैल, 2022 को इकबाल की मृत्यु हो गई। मृत्यु की तिथि को उसके निष्पादक को देय राशि ₹4,00,000 थी। 31 मार्च, 2023 से शुरू करते हुए, निष्पादक को 10% वार्षिक दर से ब्याज सहित ₹2,00,000 प्रत्येक की दो समान वार्षिक किश्तों में भुगतान किया जाना था। प्रति वर्ष 31 मार्च को खाते बंद किए जाते हैं।
इकबाल के निष्पादक के खाते का अंतिम भुगतान होने तक खाता तैयार कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
Gopal, Heera and Iqbal were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses equally. Iqbal died on 1st April, 2022. The amount payable to his executor as on the date of death amounted to ₹4,00,000. Starting from 31st March, 2023, the executor was to be paid in two equal annual instalments of ₹2,00,000 each, with interest @ 10% per annum. Accounts are closed on 31st March every year.
Prepare Iqbal's Executor's Account till it is finally settled.

key_points: Initial transfer of ₹4,00,000 to Executor's Account on 1st April 2022.
Calculate and credit interest @ 10% on outstanding balance (₹40,000) for the year ending 31st March 2023.
Record first instalment payment (Principal ₹2,00,000 + Interest ₹40,000) on 31st March 2023 and carry down balance of ₹2,00,000.
Calculate and credit interest @ 10% on remaining balance (₹20,000) for the year ending 31st March 2024.
Record final instalment payment (Principal ₹2,00,000 + Interest ₹20,000) on 31st March 2024 to settle the account.

उपर्युक्त तिथि को फर्म का विघटन हो गया तथा निम्नलिखित लेन-देन हुए :

(ii) निवेशों को उनके पुस्तक मूल्य पर 20% लाभ पर बेच दिया गया।
(iii) देनदारों से पूर्ण राशि वसूल हुई।
(iv) स्टॉक को ऋषिका द्वारा 50% बट्टे पर ले लिया गया।
(v) वसूली के वास्तविक व्यय ₹2,00,000 हुए, जिनका भुगतान फर्म द्वारा किया गया।
वसूली खाता तैयार कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
Rishika and Shivika were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3 : 2. Their Balance Sheet as at 31st March, 2024 stood as follows :
The firm was dissolved on the above date and the following transactions took place :
(i) Equipments were given to creditors in full settlement of their account.
(ii) Investments were sold at a profit of 20% on its book value.
(iii) Full amount was collected from debtors.
(iv) Stock was taken over by Rishika at 50% discount.
(v) Actual expenses of realisation amounted to ₹2,00,000 which were paid by the firm.
Prepare Realisation Account.

key_points: Transfer all assets (except Cash at Bank) to the debit side and external liabilities (Creditors) to the credit side of the Realisation A/c.

Record realisation of assets: Investments sold (₹6,00,000), Debtors realised (₹35,00,000).
Record asset taken over by partner: Stock taken by Rishika at 50% discount (₹4,00,000).
Record payment of realisation expenses: ₹2,00,000 on the debit side.
Calculate net loss on realisation and distribute it between partners in 3:2 ratio.

sub_questions.text:
अथर्व तथा अनमोल एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 5:2 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे। 31 मार्च, 2024 को उनका स्थिति विवरण निम्न प्रकार से था :
1 अप्रैल, 2024 को सूर्या को फर्म के लाभों में $\frac{2}{7}$ (मान लिया) भाग के लिए निम्नलिखित शर्तों पर एक नए साझेदार के रूप में प्रवेश दिया गया :
(i) अथर्व, अनमोल तथा सूर्या के मध्य नया लाभ विभाजन अनुपात 4 : 1 : 2 होगा।
(ii) स्थायी परिसंपत्तियों को 10% से कम करना था।
(iii) स्टॉक को ₹4,20,000 में बेच दिया गया।
(iv) सूर्या ₹3,00,000 पूँजी तथा ₹2,00,000 अपने भाग के ख्याति प्रीमियम के नकद लाएगा।
(v) पुराने साझेदारों के पूँजी खातों को नए साझेदार की पूँजी के आधार पर समायोजित किया जाएगा, जो भी स्थिति हो, पुराने साझेदारों द्वारा नकद भुगतान करके अथवा लाकर।
पुनर्मूल्यांकन खाता, साझेदारों के पूँजी खाते तथा नई फर्म का स्थिति विवरण तैयार कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english:
Atharv and Anmol were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5 : 2. Their Balance Sheet as at 31st March, 2024 was as follows :
On 1st April, 2024, Surya was admitted as a new partner for $\frac{2}{7}$ share in the profits of the firm on the following terms :
(i) The new profit sharing ratio between Atharv, Anmol and Surya will be 4 : 1 : 2. 
(ii) Fixed Assets were to be reduced by 10%.
(iii) Stock was sold at ₹4,20,000. 
(iv) Surya shall bring ₹3,00,000 as capital and ₹2,00,000 for his share of goodwill premium in cash.
(v) Capital accounts of old partners be adjusted on the basis of new partner's capital by bringing in or paying cash by the old partners, as the case may be.
Prepare Revaluation Account, Partners' Capital Accounts and the Balance Sheet of the new firm.

key_points: Prepare Revaluation A/c: Debit Fixed Assets (1,40,000). Stock was sold, leading to loss on sale or revaluation loss of 70,000. Total loss = 2,10,000.
Prepare Capital A/cs: Distribute General Reserve, Goodwill Premium, and Revaluation Loss. Calculate new capitals based on Surya's capital (3,00,000 for 2/7 share => Total Capital = 10,50,000).
Calculate cash brought in or withdrawn by Atharv and Anmol to adjust their capitals to new profit sharing ratio.
Prepare New Balance Sheet with updated Asset and Liability values, particularly adjusting the Cash balance.

sub_questions.solution:
1. Revaluation Account:
Dr.
To Fixed Assets A/c (10% of 14L) = 1,40,000
To Stock A/c (4.9L - 4.2L) = 70,000
By Loss transferred to Capitals (5:2):
  Atharv = 1,50,000
  Anmol = 60,000
Total = 2,10,000
(Note: Stock sold at 4.2L means book value drops, or realized. Given standard practice, we treat the deficit as revaluation loss).

2. Capital Accounts:
Total capital of firm = Surya's Capital * Reciprocal of share = 3,00,000 * 7/2 = 10,50,000.
New Capitals (4:1:2): Atharv = 6,00,000; Anmol = 1,50,000; Surya = 3,00,000.

Old Capitals adjusting entries:
Balances b/d: Atharv 8,00,000 | Anmol 4,00,000
Add: General Reserve (5:2): Atharv 2,50,000 | Anmol 1,00,000
Sacrifice Ratio: Old 5/7, 2/7; New 4/7, 1/7 => Sacrifice is 1/7 and 1/7 (i.e. 1:1).
Add: Goodwill Premium (1:1): Atharv 1,00,000 | Anmol 1,00,000
Less: Reval Loss: Atharv 1,50,000 | Anmol 60,000
Adjusted Capital before cash: Atharv = 10,00,000 | Anmol = 5,40,000.
Required Capital: Atharv 6,00,000 | Anmol 1,50,000.
Cash withdrawn by partners: Atharv = 4,00,000 | Anmol = 3,90,000.

3. Balance Sheet of New Firm:
Liabilities:
Creditors: 9,10,000
Capitals: Atharv 6,00,000, Anmol 1,50,000, Surya 3,00,000 = 10,50,000
Total = 19,60,000

Assets:
Fixed Assets (14L - 1.4L) = 12,60,000
Debtors = 5,60,000
Cash: 10,000 + 4,20,000 (Stock sale) + 3,00,000 (Capital) + 2,00,000 (Goodwill) - 4,00,000 (Atharv) - 3,90,000 (Anmol) = 1,40,000.
Total = 19,60,000.

चंदन, दीपक तथा एल्विश एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 1 : 2 : 2 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे। 31 मार्च, 2024 को उनका स्थिति विवरण निम्न प्रकार से था :

पुनर्मूल्यांकन खाता, साझेदारों के पूँजी खाते तथा नई फर्म का स्थिति विवरण तैयार कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english:
Chandan, Deepak and Elvish were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 1 : 2 : 2. Their Balance Sheet as at 31st March, 2024 stood as follows :
Chandan retired from the firm on 1st April, 2024 on the following terms :
(i) Fixed assets were to be depreciated by 10%.
(ii) Debtors of ₹30,000 were to be written off as bad debts.
(iii) Goodwill of the firm was valued at ₹6,00,000 and the adjustment is to be made through the accounts of the remaining partners.
(iv) Chandan was paid through cash brought in by Deepak and Elvish in such a way so as to make their capitals proportionate to their new profit sharing ratio.
Prepare Revaluation Account, Partners' Capital Accounts and the Balance Sheet of the new firm.

key_points: Prepare Revaluation A/c showing loss from depreciation of Fixed Assets and Bad debts. Distribute loss.
Adjust Goodwill: Chandan gets 1/5 of 6,00,000 = 1,20,000, borne by Deepak and Elvish equally.
Calculate Chandan's total due and transfer to Bank (Paid).
Calculate required total capital of the firm to make capitals proportionate after paying Chandan, and determine cash brought in by Deepak and Elvish.
Prepare the new Balance Sheet.

sub_questions.solution:
1. Revaluation Account:
Dr.
To Fixed Assets A/c (10% of 27L) = 2,70,000
To Bad Debts A/c = 30,000
By Loss transferred to Capitals (1:2:2):
  Chandan = 60,000
  Deepak = 1,20,000
  Elvish = 1,20,000
Total = 3,00,000

2. Partners' Capital Accounts:
Balances b/d: C = 7,00,000; D = 5,00,000; E = 3,00,000.
General Reserve (1:2:2): C = 90,000; D = 1,80,000; E = 1,80,000.
Goodwill: Chandan's share = 6,00,000 * 1/5 = 1,20,000. D and E gain equally (2:2 or 1:1).
  By D's Cap = 60,000; By E's Cap = 60,000 (in C's column).
  To C's Cap = 60,000 each (in D & E's columns).
Reval Loss: C = 60,000; D = 1,20,000; E = 1,20,000.
Chandan's Adjusted Cap (Amount due) = 7L + 90k + 1.2L - 60k = 8,50,000. Paid via Bank.
Adjusted Cap of D before cash = 5L + 1.8L - 60k - 1.2L = 5,00,000.
Adjusted Cap of E before cash = 3L + 1.8L - 60k - 1.2L = 3,00,000.
Total New Capital = D's Adj Cap + E's Adj Cap + Cash paid to C = 5L + 3L + 8.5L = 16,50,000.
New Ratio of D & E is equal (1:1). Required Cap: D = 8,25,000; E = 8,25,000.
Cash brought in: D = 8.25L - 5L = 3,25,000. E = 8.25L - 3L = 5,25,000.

3. Balance Sheet of New Firm:
Liabilities:
Creditors: 13,50,000
Capitals: Deepak 8,25,000, Elvish 8,25,000 = 16,50,000
Total = 30,00,000

Assets:
Fixed Assets (27L - 2.7L) = 24,30,000
Stock = 3,00,000
Debtors (2L - 30k) = 1,70,000
Cash (1L + 3.25L + 5.25L - 8.5L) = 1,00,000
Total = 30,00,000.

sub_questions.text_english:
Centurian Ltd. invited applications for issuing 2,00,000 equity shares of ₹10 each at a premium of ₹20 per share. The amount was payable as follows :
On Application and Allotment 
₹20 per share (including premium ₹17 per share)
On First and Final call 
₹10 per share (including premium ₹3 per share)
Applications were received for 3,00,000 equity shares and allotment was made to the applicants as follows :
Category (i) Applicants for 2,00,000 shares were allotted 1,50,000 shares.
Category (ii) Applicants for 1,00,000 shares were allotted 50,000 shares.
Excess money received on application and allotment was adjusted towards sums due on first and final call. Deepali, who had applied for 2,000 shares, failed to pay the first and final call money. Deepali belonged to Category (i). Her shares were subsequently forfeited.
Pass necessary journal entries for the above transactions in the Books of Centurion Ltd.
Open Calls-in-Arrears and Calls-in-Advance account, wherever necessary.

key_points: Record receipt of application money: 3,00,000 shares * 20 = 60,00,000.
Allotment of shares and adjustment of excess money. 2,00,000 shares issued. Total adjusted to Calls in Advance = 1,00,000 * 20 = 20,00,000.
Calculate Deepali's allotted shares and excess money. Applied = 2,000. Allotted (Category I ratio 4:3) = 1,500 shares. Excess money = 500 * 20 = 10,000.
Make Final Call due. Calculate actual amount received after adjusting Calls in Advance and Calls in Arrears (Deepali's arrears = 1,500 * 10 - 10,000 = 5,000).
Record forfeiture of Deepali's 1,500 shares.

sub_questions.solution:
Journal Entries in the books of Centurion Ltd.:

1. Bank A/c ... Dr. ₹60,00,000
     To Equity Share Application & Allotment A/c ₹60,00,000
(Being application money received for 3,00,000 shares @ ₹20)

2. Equity Share Application & Allotment A/c ... Dr. ₹60,00,000
     To Equity Share Capital A/c (2,00,000 × ₹3) ₹6,00,000
     To Securities Premium A/c (2,00,000 × ₹17) ₹34,00,000
     To Calls-in-Advance A/c (1,00,000 × ₹20) ₹20,00,000
(Being application money transferred to share capital, securities premium and excess adjusted to calls-in-advance)

3. Equity Share First & Final Call A/c ... Dr. ₹20,00,000
     To Equity Share Capital A/c (2,00,000 × ₹7) ₹14,00,000
     To Securities Premium A/c (2,00,000 × ₹3) ₹6,00,000
(Being final call made due)

4. Bank A/c ... Dr. (Balancing figure) ₹0 
   Wait, let's look at the Call. Total due = ₹20,00,000. Calls-in-Advance adjusted = ₹20,00,000. 
   The entire First & Final Call is covered by Calls-in-Advance! Let's check Category II: applied 1L, allotted 50k. Excess = 50k * 20 = 10L. Call due on 50k shares = 50k * 10 = 5L. Thus 5L excess is to be refunded. But question says "Excess money ... was adjusted towards sums due on first and final call." It doesn't explicitly mention refund, but mathematically Cat II has 5L extra even after call. 
   Let's check Deepali: Applied 2,000. Allotted 1,500. Excess = 500 * 20 = 10,000. Call due = 1,500 * 10 = 15,000. Arrears = 15,000 - 10,000 = 5,000.
   Since Calls-in-Advance total was ₹20,00,000 and total call due is ₹20,00,000, no one needs to pay except Deepali's shortfall. 
   Entry for adjustment:
   Calls-in-Advance A/c ... Dr. ₹19,95,000
   Calls-in-Arrears A/c ... Dr. ₹5,000
     To Equity Share First & Final Call A/c ₹20,00,000
(Being Calls-in-advance adjusted and arrears recorded)

5. Equity Share Capital A/c (1,500 × ₹10) ... Dr. ₹15,000
   Securities Premium A/c (1,500 × ₹3) ... Dr. ₹4,500 
   (Premium on allotment is already received. Premium on call is unpaid, so we reverse it. The excess ₹10,000 covers the call's capital portion ₹10,500 mostly. Let's assume premium is unpaid).
     To Calls-in-Arrears A/c ₹5,000
     To Share Forfeiture A/c ₹14,500
(Being 1,500 shares of Deepali forfeited for non-payment of call)

From the following information, calculate Interest Coverage Ratio :

| Particulars | Amount (₹) |
|---|---|
| Profit after Tax | 6,30,000 |
| Tax Rate | 30% |
| 15% Debentures | 20,00,000 |
| Equity Share Capital | 10,00,000 |

key_points: Calculate Interest on Debentures: 15% of ₹20,00,000 = ₹3,00,000.
Calculate Profit before Tax (PBT): PAT / (1 - Tax Rate) = ₹6,30,000 / 0.70 = ₹9,00,000.
Calculate Profit Before Interest and Tax (PBIT): PBT + Interest = ₹9,00,000 + ₹3,00,000 = ₹12,00,000.
Calculate Interest Coverage Ratio: PBIT / Interest = ₹12,00,000 / ₹3,00,000 = 4 Times.

sub_questions.solution:
Working Notes:
1. Interest on 15% Debentures = 15% of ₹20,00,000 = ₹3,00,000.
2. Profit before Tax (PBT):
   Since the tax rate is 30%, Profit after Tax represents 70% of the Profit before Tax.
   PBT = Profit after Tax × (100 / 70) = ₹6,30,000 × (100 / 70) = ₹9,00,000.
3. Profit before Interest and Tax (PBIT):
   PBIT = Profit before Tax + Interest on Long-Term Debt
   PBIT = ₹9,00,000 + ₹3,00,000 = ₹12,00,000.

Calculation of Interest Coverage Ratio:
Interest Coverage Ratio = Profit before Interest and Tax (PBIT) / Interest on Long-Term Debt
Interest Coverage Ratio = ₹12,00,000 / ₹3,00,000
= 4 Times.

sub_questions.text_english:
Calculate the amount of Opening Trade Receivables and Closing Trade Receivables from the following information :
Trade Receivables Turnover Ratio = 5 times
Cost of Revenue from operations = ₹8,00,000
Gross Profit Ratio = 20%
Closing Trade Receivables were ₹40,000 more than that in the beginning.
Cash sales were $\frac{1}{4}$th of Credit sales.

key_points: Calculate Total Revenue: Gross Profit is 20% of Revenue, meaning Cost is 80%. Revenue = 8,00,000 / 0.80 = 10,00,000.
Calculate Credit Revenue: Let Credit Sales be x. Cash sales = 0.25x. Total Sales = x + 0.25x = 1.25x. 1.25x = 10,00,000 => Credit Sales = 8,00,000.
Calculate Average Trade Receivables: TR Turnover Ratio = Credit Revenue / Average TR. 5 = 8,00,000 / Avg TR => Avg TR = 1,60,000.
Calculate Opening and Closing TR: (Open + Close) / 2 = 1,60,000 => Open + Close = 3,20,000. Close = Open + 40,000. => 2*Open + 40,000 = 3,20,000 => Opening TR = 1,40,000. Closing TR = 1,80,000.

sub_questions.solution:
Working Notes:
1. Calculation of Total Revenue from Operations (Net Sales):
   Gross Profit Ratio = 20% of Net Sales.
   Therefore, Cost of Revenue from Operations = 80% of Net Sales.
   Net Sales = (Cost of Revenue from Operations / 80) × 100
   Net Sales = (₹8,00,000 / 80) × 100 = ₹10,00,000.

2. Calculation of Credit Sales:
   Let Credit Sales = x
   Cash Sales = $\frac{1}{4}$ of x = 0.25x
   Total Sales = Cash Sales + Credit Sales

   Closing TR = ₹1,40,000 + ₹40,000 = ₹1,80,000.

questions.text_english: Differentiate between tailored and specific softwares on any three basis.

key_points: Nature/Definition: Tailored is built exclusively for one organization's unique needs. Specific software is built for a specific industry/purpose but sold to multiple buyers.
Cost: Tailored software is highly expensive due to custom development. Specific software is moderately priced as costs are shared among many buyers.
Time: Tailored takes a long time to develop and implement. Specific software is generally ready to deploy much faster.

questions.solution:
Tailored and specific software can be differentiated on the following three bases:
1. Nature: Tailored (customized) software is developed exclusively to meet the specific and unique requirements of a single organization. In contrast, specific software is developed for a particular industry or niche market (like hotel management or hospital billing) and is sold to multiple users in that sector.
2. Cost: Tailored software involves high development and maintenance costs since it is built from scratch for one client. Specific software is relatively less expensive because the development cost is distributed among many purchasers.
3. Implementation Time: Developing tailored software is a time-consuming process that requires extensive coding and testing. Specific software is generally available off-the-shelf for that industry and requires much less time to deploy.

Automatic Posting to Ledgers.
Auto-generation of Trial Balance.
Preparation of Final Accounts (Trading, P&L, Balance Sheet) instantaneously.

sub_questions.solution:
The accounting cycle comprises a systematic process of recording and reporting financial data, most of which can be fully automated using computers. 
Firstly, Data Entry (Journalizing) is done where transactions are recorded via electronic vouchers. 
Secondly, the system performs Automatic Posting. Unlike manual accounting, once data is entered, the computer instantly posts the entries to the respective ledger accounts without human intervention.
Thirdly, the system automatically generates a Trial Balance at any given point in time, ensuring mathematical accuracy seamlessly.
Finally, the computer processes these balances to instantaneously prepare the Final Financial Statements, including the Statement of Profit and Loss and the Balance Sheet, providing real-time financial reporting.
